title: Emergency communication checklist and stakeholder matrix
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic runbook for incident communications: short internal war-room checklist, a stakeholder matrix (who to notify and when), and short-ready-to-send status page / customer update snippets. This is a working draft for on-call SREs and incident leads; intended for rapid adaptation during incidents and for sync with CS/PR/legal when needed.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to platform outages, degraded serving performance (high 95th/99th latency), and ingress failures affecting hosted API and Dedicated control plane.
- Not intended for scheduled maintenance communications (see maintenance playbook).
- Use plain language for external comms; include technical detail only when it helps customers understand impact and mitigation steps.

Incident severity quick guide (for comm cadence):
- Sev 1: Global outage impacting >20% customers or major revenue paths. High urgency.
- Sev 2: Partial outage, degraded performance, or major feature broken for a subset. Moderate urgency.
- Sev 3: Localized issue, minor degradation, non-critical feature. Low urgency.

Stakeholder matrix (who to notify, trigger, and channel):
- On-call SRE (automatic): immediate; PagerDuty -> Slack #sre-incident -> create incident thread.
- SRE Lead / Incident Commander: on escalation to Sev2/Sev1; Slack + phone if after hours.
- Engineering owner (service team): on detection; Slack and assign ticket.
- Customer Success (CS): when customers are impacted or tickets appear; Slack DM and email summary for major incidents.
- Support / CS Ops: when >5 customer tickets or proactive outreach needed; Slack + spreadsheet for outreach tracking.
- Product / Execs: for Sev1 or high-visibility incidents; 15-min summary via Slack and optional daily exec update.
- Legal / Compliance: for incidents involving data exposure or legal obligations; notify immediately via secure channel.
- PR/Comms: for public-facing incidents with expected customer interest or press; coordinate message and timing.

Channels and templates to use (internal):
- Slack incident channel: create #incident-<shortid>-<svc> (e.g., #incident-2048-hosted-api). Post pinned summary every 30m.
- Incident doc: start a one-page incident doc in confluence / google doc with timeline, owners, mitigations, customer impact and next actions.
- War-room checklist (first 30 minutes):
  1) Confirm and document scope: affected services, regions, customer-facing features.
  2) Triage severity and assign IC and scribe.
  3) Ensure monitoring links, runbooks, and recent deploys are attached to the doc.
  4) Post initial internal note: "Investigation underway" (see internal snippet below).
  5) Notify CS about impacted customers and open channels for inbound tickets.
  6) Begin short-term mitigation attempts and document each action.

War-room checklist (ongoing):
- Maintain a rolling timeline in the incident doc with timestamps for every action and message.
- Update Slack pinned message every 15-30 minutes for Sev1, every 60 minutes for Sev2.
- If a rollback or circuit-breaker is used, add a short customer-facing snippet immediately.
- Track customer outreach in a shared spreadsheet: customer name, contact, impact, outreach owner, status.

Internal communication snippets (copy-and-paste friendly):
- Initial internal (post-detection):
  "[<TIME>] Detected increased error rate for <service>. Triage in progress. IC: <name>. Scribe: <name>. Scope: customers in <region/zone> may see failures. More updates in <incident-channel> and incident doc: <link>."

- 30-min checkpoint (internal):
  "[<TIME>] Checkpoint: we have identified <root-candidate/area>. Mitigation steps underway: <short list>. ETA for next update: <minutes>. Customer impact: <summary>."

External / status page templates (short):
- Investigating (short, public):
  "We are aware of an issue affecting <product area>. Our team is investigating and working to restore normal service. We will provide updates here and via email to affected customers. "

- Mitigating (public):
  "We have identified the cause affecting <feature> and are applying mitigations. Customers may experience intermittent errors or higher latency. We will continue to monitor and update."

- Partial degradation (public, when mitigations reduce but not fully resolved):
  "Service is partially restored; some customers may still see degraded performance. We are actively working on full resolution and expect further updates in <ETA>."

- Resolved (public):
  "The issue impacting <feature> has been resolved. Normal service has been restored as of <time>. If you continue to see problems, please contact support."

Customer direct message / email (template for CS outreach):
Subject: Incident: <short summary> — <Impact level>
Body:
  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We wanted to let you know we experienced an incident affecting <service/feature> between <start> and <end or ongoing>. Impact: <what they might have seen>.

  What we did: <one-sentence mitigation>. Next steps: <what we're doing to prevent recurrence>.

  If you need realtime updates or help, reply to this thread or open a ticket and we'll prioritize.

  Apologies for the disruption,
  <Customer Success rep> on behalf of Redwood Inference

Tone and content guidance for external messages:
- Keep it short and factual. Avoid internal jargon.
- Do not speculate about causes or root cause in early updates. Use "investigating" and "mitigating" language.
- When possible, include workarounds customers can apply.
- Escalate to PR/Comms for any message that might be shared externally beyond customer list or that may attract press.

Timing matrix for public updates (recommended):
- Sev1: Post initial status page within 15 minutes, then every 30 minutes until resolved or stable.
- Sev2: Initial status page within 30–60 minutes, then hourly until resolved.
- Sev3: Update if there is material customer impact or on resolution.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Incident Commander (IC): single decision-maker for communications cadence and major mitigations.
- Scribe: maintain timeline, post updates to status page and incident channel.
- Eng owner: run fixes and coordinate rollbacks.
- CS lead: own customer outreach and provide recipient list.
- PR/Comms: approve external messaging for broad distribution.
- Legal: advise on disclosures for breaches or regulated data.

Post-incident comms checklist (first 24 hours):
1) Publish a brief "incident resolved" note on status page with timeframe and impact summary.
2) CS sends an email to affected customers with a plain-English summary and next steps.
3) IC ensures a postmortem doc is started and assigned (attach timeline and communications record).
4) PR/Comms drafts any public postmortem for high-profile incidents.
5) Schedule postmortem review with all stakeholders within 72 hours.

Template: post-incident summary (internal):
- Title: Incident <id> — <short title>
- Severity: SevX
- Start: <time> End: <time>
- Impact: <concise list of affected services/customers>
- Root cause (initial): <if known or "under investigation">
- Mitigation: <actions taken>
- Customer communications: <links to status page and sent emails>
- Action items: <list owners and ETA>

Notes, open questions and TODOs for this draft:
- Add machine-readable checklist for automated paging from monitoring alerts.
- Create a small library of customer-friendly workarounds for common issues (cache clear steps, retry guidance).
- Align timing cadence with CS availability in APAC regions.
- Confirm legal notify thresholds for EU customers (data regs).

Appendix: quick copy variants for status page (one-liners)
- "Investigating: experiencing elevated errors for <service>."
- "Mitigating: applying fixes to restore normal service; some requests may fail."
- "Resolved: system operating normally as of <time>."

-- End of draft --

Author notes: keep this doc lightweight. We will fold validated templates into the official ops runbook and status page automation once the wording is approved by PR and CS.
